templates.pattern: A wave has a time period of [T] ms. What is its frequency in Hz?
A source emits sound at [F] Hz and moves toward a stationary observer at [VS] m/s. The speed of sound is [V] m/s. What is the observed frequency?
templates.explanation: Doppler effect (source approaching): f' = f × v ÷ (v − vs) = [F] × [V] ÷ ([V] − [VS]) = [F*V] ÷ [V-VS] = [RESULT] Hz

templates.pattern: A source emits sound at [F] Hz and moves away from a stationary observer at [VS] m/s. The speed of sound is [V] m/s. What is the observed frequency?
templates.explanation: Doppler effect (source receding): f' = f × v ÷ (v + vs) = [F] × [V] ÷ ([V] + [VS]) = [F*V] ÷ [V+VS] = [RESULT] Hz

templates.pattern: A standing wave is set up on a string of length [L] m. What is the wavelength of the fundamental frequency (first harmonic)?
templates.explanation: For the fundamental frequency on a string fixed at both ends, wavelength = 2 × length = 2 × [L] = [RESULT] m

templates.pattern: A string of length [L] m has a wave speed of [V] m/s. What is its fundamental frequency?
Sound intensity at distance [D1] m from a source is [I] W/m². What is the intensity at distance [D2] m? (inverse square law)
templates.explanation: Inverse square law: I₁d₁² = I₂d₂² → I₂ = I₁×d₁² ÷ d₂² = [I]×[D1]² ÷ [D2]² = [I*D1*D1] ÷ [D2*D2] = [RESULT] W/m²

templates.pattern: A wave refracts as it crosses a boundary. Its speed changes from [V1] m/s to [V2] m/s. If the original wavelength was [L1] m, what is the new wavelength?
templates.explanation: Frequency stays constant at a boundary. λ₂ = λ₁ × v₂ ÷ v₁ = [L1] × [V2] ÷ [V1] = [RESULT] m

templates.pattern: Two speakers emit the same frequency of [F] Hz in phase. At a certain point the path difference is [PD] m. The speed of sound is 340 m/s. Is it constructive or destructive interference?
templates.explanation: Wavelength = 340 ÷ [F] m. If path difference = whole number of wavelengths → constructive. If half wavelength → destructive.

templates.pattern: A pipe open at both ends has a length of [L] m. The speed of sound is 340 m/s. What is the fundamental frequency of the pipe?
templates.explanation: For an open pipe, fundamental frequency f = v ÷ 2L = 340 ÷ (2 × [L]) = 340 ÷ [2*L] = [RESULT] Hz

templates.pattern: A pipe closed at one end has a length of [L] m. The speed of sound is 340 m/s. What is the fundamental frequency?
templates.explanation: For a closed pipe, fundamental frequency f = v ÷ 4L = 340 ÷ (4 × [L]) = 340 ÷ [4*L] = [RESULT] Hz
